_comment: Judgment calls the files themselves cannot tell. `default` applies to any name not listed. Where the declaring file already says (setup.py install_requires = run, requirements.dev = test), this file is not used.

apt_commands._comment: apt commands the Dockerfile does not contain, because a script runs them, matched by a part of the command line. The nodesource setup script installs these only so that nodejs, which the tests need, can be installed.

ship._comment: Dependencies whose code is linked into a native library we distribute: '<ecosystem>:<name>' -> ids of the components the NOTICE files list (the `# attribution:` comments). An id is the last part of a row's package name in cpp/NOTICE, lower case, `_` as `-` (`boringssl/third_party/fiat` is `fiat`). `collect.py check` fails when a key matches nothing.

licenses._comment: The license of a dependency nothing else names: '<ecosystem>:<name>' -> an SPDX expression, or {"license": ..., "url": the license text}. A dependency linked into a native library takes its license from third_party_notices/components.json first. An entry here overrides what a pip, npm, apt or Bazel package says about itself, so use it for what the package cannot name. A license that is not a common one needs a `url`. The license is what the project's own license file says, read on the date in the commit; it is not a legal review.

git:aws-lc.license: Apache-2.0 OR ISC (code derived from BoringSSL and OpenSSL keeps its own licenses)

licenses.apt:libcrypt-dev: LGPL-2.1-or-later (the overall license of libxcrypt; many files carry other licenses, see the package's copyright file)

apt:libssl-dev.license: OpenSSL AND SSLeay (both licenses apply, as the package's copyright file says)

apt:libssl1.1.license: OpenSSL AND SSLeay (both licenses apply, as the package's copyright file says)

apt:openssl.license: OpenSSL AND SSLeay (both licenses apply, as the package's copyright file says)

licenses.apt:libx11-6: MIT (the X.Org standard copyright, a variant of the MIT license; some files carry other licenses, see each source file)
licenses.apt:libx11-data: MIT (the X.Org standard copyright, a variant of the MIT license; some files carry other licenses, see each source file)
licenses.apt:nodejs: MIT (Node.js; the third-party components bundled in it carry their own licenses, listed in its copyright file)
licenses.apt:python3-distutils: PSF-2.0 (the Python license; the incorporated software carries its own licenses)
licenses.apt:python3-lib2to3: PSF-2.0 (the Python license; the incorporated software carries its own licenses)

license_urls._comment: A link to the text of a license that a package names by an identifier that is not a common one, so that the table can give the link a review asks for. Matched against each name of the license expression.

coverage._comment: `collect.py check` looks for tracked files that download or install something (curl or wget with a URL, git clone, pip or npm or apt-get install, FROM, http_archive) and fails on any file the collector does not read. List a file here only when it is covered another way or is not an input of the build. Patterns are shell globs on the path from the repository root; `*` also matches `/`.

resolved_at_test_time._comment: Scripts of the real-GPU tests (tests/gpu) that install Python packages and apt packages inside the test container when it runs: torch, numpy, boto3 and the streamer wheels, resolved at that time from the requirement specs the run passes in (a nightly run takes the newest torch). Their images are listed from tests/gpu/compose.yaml; the packages are not listed, because what pip resolves is known only when the tests run, and the same packages are listed in the test group from py/*/Makefile.

allowed_commands._comment: A file the collector reads can hold a command of a kind it does not read (for example a workflow step that runs `pip install`). List it here as '<path glob>': {"kinds": ["<kind>"], "reason": "<why it is not an input of the build>"}. The kinds are the keys of COMMANDS in completeness.py.

tests/*/compose*.y*ml.reason: the health check of a service runs wget against localhost inside the container; it downloads nothing
